How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow
all speakers to address the City Council. Please note that interactions between the City
Council, City staff, and the public during meetings are subject to the City’s Rules of
Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – MAY 2025

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2024-2025 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 24-35) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2024-2025 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for May 2025.

  D. MEASURE R FUNDING AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 1 WITH THE LOS
  ANGELES METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (LA METRO)
  FOR THE SAN GABRIEL ADAPTIVE/TRAFFIC RESPONSIVE SIGNAL
  CONTROL PROJECT (MR5.3.1.10) AND TRAFFIC SIGNAL IMPROVEMENTS
  PROJECT (MR5.3.2.21)

  The Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LA Metro)
  approved seven projects in the City to alleviate traffic congestion caused by the
  cancellation of State Route-710 construction between the Interstate-10 and
  Interstate-210. Two of the seven approved projects are Intelligent
  Transportation Systems initiatives, for which the City entered into funding
  agreements with LA Metro to accept $3,830,000 in Measure R Funds in 2020.
  The funding agreement amendments will have no impact on the General Fund
  and will provide an additional $3,900,000 in Measure R Highway Funds for both
  projects. The City must spend local funds first and then become reimbursed by
  LA Metro on a quarterly basis. Funding for both projects is programmed in the
  adopted Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Capital Improvement Program, specifying

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 17, 2025  3
   Measure R funds. These funds will be reimbursed quarterly as the projects
  progress.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378(b)(4) of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Mayor to execute the
  funding agreements on behalf of the City, approving funding agreement
  amendments FA#9200000000MR53110 and FA#9200000000MR53221 with Los
  Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA) to accept an
  additional $3,900,000 in Measure R funds for the San Gabriel Adaptive/Traffic
  Signal Control Project (CIP 2-21-01) and the San Gabriel Traffic Signal
  Improvement Project (CIP 2-21-02), with reimbursement provided through
  LACMTA Quarterly Expenditure Reports.

  E. ANNUAL RATE REVIEW AND ADJUSTMENTS FOR WASTE AND STREET
  SWEEPING SERVICES WITH ATHENS SERVICES FOR $11,432.16 MONTHLY

  For many years, the City has contracted with Athens Services for street
  sweeping and waste services. In July 2021, the City Council approved a rate
  schedule to incorporate mandated organics recycling and merge the street
  sweeping and waste services contracts. In accordance with the Sixth
  Amendment to the contract for services dated July 6, 2021, Athens Services has
  submitted two requests for City Council approval to adjust the rates for street
  sweeping and waste services. These adjustments are based on applicable
  Consumer Price Indices (CPI), with the changes set to take effect on July 1, 2025.
  The Fiscal Year 2025-2026 adopted budget for street sweeping services is
  $137,185.92, which includes the proposed increase which would be funded by
  Gas Tax account 136-800-02-22-055.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the annual rate adjustments proposed by Athens Services, as
  outlined in the attached rate schedules, effective July 1, 2025.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 17, 2025  4
   2. Authorize the City Manager to approve a purchase order with Athens
  Services for $137,185.92 for street sweeping services, funded by Gas Tax
  account 136-800-02-22-055.

  F. ORDINANCE NO. 719: ADOPTION OF CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF
  FORESTRY AND FIRE PROTECTION FIRE HAZARD SEVERITY ZONE MAP –
  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  Ordinance No. 719 will adopt the California Department of Forestry and Fire
  Protection Fire Hazard Severity Zone maps for Local Responsibility Areas, in
  accordance with California Government Code Section 51179. Ordinance No.
  719 was introduced and the first reading was conducted by title only by a 5-0
  vote of the City Council at the June 3, 2025 City Council meeting. The Fiscal Year
  2024-2025 Adopted Budget includes the cost for required legal publication
  (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and codification (Account No. 121-702-00-
  22-000) of the ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The adoption of the
  updated Fire Hazard Severity Zone map is exempt from CEQA Guidelines under
  Section 15061(b)(3).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 719, adding Chapter 96 “Fire Protection and Prevention” to Title IX “General
  Regulations” of the San Gabriel Municipal Code.

  G. AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY HUMANE SOCIETY (SGVHS)
  FOR ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL SERVICES FOR FY 2025-2026 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $590,500

  The San Gabriel Valley Humane Society (SGVHS) had provided animal care and
  control services to the community for many decades. The City’s most recent
  agreement with SGVHS was approved by the City Council on June 4, 2024. The
  SGVHS is requesting to continue services for the City for Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-
  2026. The cost to the City for SGVHS to provide a full-service animal care and
  control program for FY 2025-2026 is $590,500 and is included in the adopted
  FY 2025-2026 budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 17, 2025  5
   Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the agreement with the San Gabriel Valley Humane Society for Fiscal Year 2025-
  2026 in the amount of $590,500.

  H. APPROVAL OF MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH SAN GABRIEL
  UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR USE OF GABRIELINO HIGH SCHOOL
  CAMPUS FOR INDEPENDENCE DAY CELEBRATION

  The City of San Gabriel will hold its Independence Day Celebration on Thursday,
  July 3, 2025. The event will include entertainment, games, food trucks,
  community booths and will conclude with a drone, laser and light show. The
  Independence Day Celebration will be held at Gabrielino High School. Any
  District custodial work needed for the City’s use of the property will be billed at
  $40 per hour. This amount will be covered by the Non-Departmental account
  for special events.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Gabrielino High School as the location for the Independence Day
  Celebration; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to sign the Memorandum of Understanding
  with San Gabriel Unified School District for this purpose.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. APPROVAL OF AGREEMENT WITH DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH FOR
  HEALTH OFFICER SERVICES – 2ND READING & ADOPTION [ORDINANCE
  NO. 720]

  The City of San Gabriel uses the Los Angeles County Public Health Code as the
  “Health Code” for the City. The Los Angeles County Department of Public
  Health approached all 85 cities within Los Angeles County, including San
  Gabriel, about updating the agreement that provides updated public health
  services for cities. At its regular meeting on June 3, 2025, the City Council
  introduced Ordinance 720, conducted a first reading by title only, scheduled a
  public hearing, second reading, and adoption for the next regular meeting.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 17, 2025  6
   Generally, the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health administers
  local public health services to the City of San Gabriel and other municipalities
  at no cost. Any costs for inspection services requested by the City will be done
  within current budgets. There is no fiscal impact resulting from the adoption of
  the proposed ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing.

  2. Approve the Agreement with Los Angeles County for Public Health Services
  and authorize the City Manager to execute the Agreement.

  3. Waive reading and adopt Ordinance No. 720.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AGREEMENT WITH DAVID VOLZ DESIGN, INCORPORATED FOR CONCEPT
  DESIGN DEVELOPMENT FOR THE SAN GABRIEL VETERANS MEMORIAL IN
  AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $35,461 AND RESOLUTION NO. 25-28
  APPROPRIATING $35,461 FOR CONCEPT DESIGN DEVELOPMENT

  For the past several years, the City has been placing 200 flags in Plaza Park as
  part of a Field of Heroes to honor Veterans in our community. In addition, the
  City has held Veterans Day and Memorial Day ceremonies, which have been
  well received by the community. In addition to these items, City Council has
  expressed an interest in having a permanent Veterans Memorial that will be
  accessible year-round for residents and visitors to reflect on the dedication of
  our community’s Veterans. The flags will continue to be placed and ceremonies
  held in honor of Memorial Day and Veterans Day when the permanent
  memorial is in place. Additionally, the City has partnered with the San Gabriel
  Veterans’ Memorial Coalition (SGVMC), a nonprofit group established in 2020
  for the purpose of honoring San Gabriel’s veterans and working toward the
  development of a memorial in San Gabriel. In July 2024, the City Council
  approved the location of the City’s future Veterans Memorial in Plaza Park. The
  project will honor the branches of the military – Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 17, 2025  7
   Corps, Space Force and Coast Guard and serve as a memorial for San Gabriel’s
  veterans. SGVMC also has an interest in including the names of those who
  served. David Volz Design, Incorporated’s fee for conceptual design
  development is $35,461. The City Council will need to appropriate funding from
  the City’s Park Development Impact Fees since this is expansion/creation of a
  park feature. Appropriated funds would be reallocated into Special Project
  account #124-850-40-97-821.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the agreement with David Volz Design, Incorporated for the
  conceptual design development phase for San Gabriel’s Veterans Memorial;

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any other
  necessary documents pending review and approval by the City Attorney;

  3. Designate two City Councilmembers to serve as the lead Council contacts
  for this planning process; and

  4. Adopt Resolution No. 25-28 appropriating $35,461 from the City’s Park
  Development Impact Fees into account #124-850-40-97-821 for Memorial
  Conceptual Design Development.

  B. UPDATE ON THE RIDESG SERVICE AND AWARD OF AGREEMENT WITH
  LAZ PARKING CALIFORNIA LLC FOR CONTRACT OPERATIONS FOR
  MICROTRANSIT TRANSPORTATION SERVICES (RIDESG) IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $817,258.00 FOR THE FIRST YEAR

  The City of San Gabriel operates an on-demand micro transit service, RideSG.
  The program allows residents and visitors alike to travel anywhere within the
  City of San Gabriel. Additional benefits are available through the RideSG Plus
  membership for residents 62 years of age and older and residents with a
  disability. At the November 19, 2024 City Council meeting, the Council adopted
  changes to the service including expanded service hours and changes to the
  use parameters for RideSG Plus riders. The contract with the City’s current
  provider, TransDev, will expire on June 30. As approved by City Council on June
  3, 2025, the RideSG account number (181-850-49-81-000) has $858,890
  allocated for Fiscal Year 2025-2026. These funds are restricted for

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 17, 2025  8
   transportation services. The contract with LAZ Parking California, LLC to operate
  the microtransit transportation services (RideSG) is $817,258 for the first year,
  resulting in a budget savings of $41,632. The only additional cost under the
  contract is a nominal fee charged of $5.96 per call for customer service support
  provided outside of City staff hours.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the professional services agreement with LAZ Parking California, LLC and any
  other necessary documents pending review and approval by the City Attorney.

  Alternatives to Staff Recommendations:

  1. Select another vendor from the list of responders.

  2. Send the item back to staff to determine additional alternatives.

  3. Other options that the City Council determines after discussing the item.

  8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of

  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, July 1, 2025, at
